editorial:
Ever wonder how a tiny news team manages to land a massive interview with a royal who doesn't want to talk? You get to follow the smart, driven women at Newsnight as they play a high-stakes game of cat and mouse with Prince Andrew. The vibe is like a fast-paced office drama where the tension builds every time someone picks up the phone. You will feel the stress and the excitement as they try to trick the royal palace into agreeing to a sit-down meeting that could change everything.

What really makes this work is the acting, especially the lead who plays the reporter. She makes the boring parts of journalism feel like a thriller. The pacing is snappy, though some of the talking scenes might feel a bit long if you aren't into politics. If you enjoy seeing a group of underdogs win, you will love this. To get the best experience, you should stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video for those crisp details, or you can rent it on Apple TV for a quick movie night with friends.
endingExplained: The movie wraps up with the actual interview taking place, where Prince Andrew gives answers that make him look even worse. You see the news team celebrate their huge win as the footage goes viral globally. The final scenes show the fallout of the interview, confirming that the royal family had to distance themselves from him. It ends with a feeling of victory for the journalists who worked so hard to get the truth out.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves royal scandals and behind-the-scenes news stories.
